_about: The first scheme built on a faction. `play.conflicts` gives every world five of
them with a `wants`, a `works_by`, a `holds` and an `undone_by`, and only the
shipped line's patron had ever used one — as a paymaster, off-stage, never named
to the player. Here the guild is the thing the quest is about, and its own
`undone_by` is what is inside the letter.
It opens at the guildhall, which no scheme had used for anything, and it is the
only scheme where the player is never asked to fight, steal, or find anybody. The
whole decision is whether to carry a sealed thing to the person it is addressed to
after finding out what it does.
The faction slot is text and nothing else. It has no `ref` — it is a row out of the
export, not a body on the board — so it can be named in a card or a tell and can
never be granted an attitude, moved, or killed.

schemes.title: The sealed letter
schemes.about: A guild pays well for a fast pair of legs, and does not say what is in the packet.

cards.title: Carry $clerk's packet out to $reader
cards.reward: paid at $guildhall on your word that it arrived

cards.title: What is inside $clerk's packet
facts: It is the thing that undoes $guild, written out plainly, and $reader is the one person who would act on it.
$clerk is not betraying anybody: $clerk was told to send it and was not told what it was.

grants_on_open.say: $clerk watched your hands until the packet was out of sight, and then stopped watching

action.says: $guild is paying at $guildhall for a fast pair of legs and asking no questions about them.

tell.perceptible: The notice is up at $guildhall, in $guild's own hand.
Nobody at $gate asks what is in the packet.

action.text: The packet is not a bill of lading. It is the one thing that would undo $guild, and $reader is who it is addressed to.

tell.perceptible: Out on $road the seal has already gone soft, and what is written inside is not freight.
$reader takes it, reads it twice, and asks who else has seen it.
$clerk takes the packet back at $guildhall and does not look at it.
